findings.issue_text: Team permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both team admin and owner, incorrectly denying admins who are not owners
sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added email
EventManager is constructed from ctx.user credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar updates fail or target the wrong calendar when a non-organizer adds guests
catch around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows the error and logs only a static string, discarding err and making failures invisible in production

Guest dedup and blacklist email checks are case-sensitive since guest emails are not lowercased, allowing BlockedList@Example.com to bypass the blacklist and treating case-variant emails as distinct duplicates

The evt CalendarEvent never sets the team field, but sendAddGuestsEmails iterates calendarEvent.team?.members to send team-member emails, making that branch dead code so team members never receive notifications

Duplicate-attendee filter and createMany are separate non-transactional operations, allowing concurrent requests to create duplicate attendee rows with no transaction or unique constraint guarding them
For seated bookings with seatsPerTimeSlot, the handler creates raw attendee rows via createMany, bypassing seat-count limits and the BookingSeat model, potentially overbooking the event
isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog is set to true on validation failure but never reset to false when input is fixed, leaving a stale error after successful mutation and when the dialog is reopened

AddGuestsDialog initial state has an empty email field, so clicking Add without typing shows a validation error instead of a no-op, and removing all fields makes the button silently do nothing; empty strings should be trimmed/filtered before validating
No tests added for addGuests.handler.ts permission matrix, blacklist filtering, duplicate handling, addGuests.schema.ts, or the new MultiEmail component

AddGuestsDialog is mounted for every booking in BookingListItem regardless of user permission, and the additional_guests menu item is shown unconditionally instead of being gated by handler permission rules

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added email

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-existing attendee emails and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However, it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw, unfiltered `guests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, attendees whose email is included in the provided `newGuests` array receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the caller includes an email that is already an attendee (filtered out from `uniqueGuests` but still present in `guests`), that existing attendee will incorrectly receive the full scheduled email rather than the “guests added” email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so calendar updates fail or target the wrong calendar when a non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code builds the `EventManager` using `ctx.user` (the authenticated caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. However, the booking’s organizer is `booking.userId`/`booking.user` (organizer data is even fetched separately as `organizer`). If a team admin/owner or an attendee (non-organizer) triggers `addGuests`, the calendar update call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run with the caller’s credentials/user context instead of the organizer’s, which can fail (no creds) or update the wrong calendar account. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: catch around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows the error and logs only a static string, discarding err and making failures invisible in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` where the `catch (err)` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log/propagate `err` or return an error. This demonstrably discards the actual exception details and allows the mutation to succeed even when email sending fails, reducing visibility into failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The evt CalendarEvent never sets the team field, but sendAddGuestsEmails iterates calendarEvent.team?.members to send team-member emails, making that branch dead code so team members never receive notifications

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes `organizer`, `attendees`, `uid`, etc., but never sets any `team` property (nor does the booking query include team/member data). In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does `const calendarEvent = formatCalEvent(calEvent);` and then conditionally iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to send `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` to each team member. Since `evt.team` is never populated in this diff, `calendarEvent.team?.members` will be undefined/absent and that loop will not run, so team members won’t receive the intended notifications for team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee filter and createMany are separate non-transactional operations, allowing concurrent requests to create duplicate attendee rows with no transaction or unique constraint guarding them

adjudication.rationale: The handler does perform a read (findFirst include attendees) followed by a write (booking.update createMany) without wrapping them in a transaction, so there is a potential race between concurrent requests. However, the finding asserts that this “allows … duplicate attendee rows” specifically because there is “no … unique constraint guarding them,” and the absence of a DB uniqueness constraint is not verifiable from this diff. With a unique constraint, the race would likely result in a constraint violation rather than duplicated rows. Therefore the proposed finding overclaims beyond what the diff alone establishes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For seated bookings with seatsPerTimeSlot, the handler creates raw attendee rows via createMany, bypassing seat-count limits and the BookingSeat model, potentially overbooking the event

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new `booking.attendees` rows via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (which is explicitly present on the booking/event and later copied into the `CalendarEvent` as `evt.seatsPerTimeSlot`). There is no validation against a maximum seat count or any other capacity constraint before adding guests, so for seat-limited events this endpoint can increase the attendee count beyond the allowed seats (i.e., overbook). Whether a separate `BookingSeat` model exists isn’t shown in the diff, but the lack of any seat-limit enforcement for `seatsPerTimeSlot` is directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog is set to true on validation failure but never reset to false when input is fixed, leaving a stale error after successful mutation and when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: `AddGuestsDialog` initializes `isInvalidEmail` to `false` and sets it to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse` fails in `handleAdd()`. However, it is not reset to `false` when validation later succeeds (before calling `addGuestsMutation.mutate`) nor in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Since the dialog component remains mounted in `BookingListItem` even when closed, reopening it can show the stale error message (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`), and the error can also remain visible while a now-valid submission is pending.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests added for addGuests.handler.ts permission matrix, blacklist filtering, duplicate handling, addGuests.schema.ts, or the new MultiEmail component

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (TRPC addGuests handler/schema, dialogs, MultiEmail, email templates) but it does not show any accompanying test additions. However, “no tests added” is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete defect, bug, or security/correctness issue that can be verified from the diff alone. The finding also assumes required test coverage expectations that are not established by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog is mounted for every booking in BookingListItem regardless of user permission, and the additional_guests menu item is shown unconditionally instead of being gated by handler permission rules

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an "additional_guests" action and mounts `<AddGuestsDialog />` unconditionally inside `BookingListItem`, but nothing in the diff establishes that `BookingListItem` can be rendered for users who lack permission for that booking. Also, the new backend handler explicitly allows organizers *or attendees* (and some team roles) to add guests, so a UI gate isn’t clearly required by the handler rules. Mounting a closed dialog per item is a performance/UX consideration at most, not a verifiable permission/security defect from this diff alone.
